agent_notes: Bhanabasti returns almost nothing in open web/news/social/video/image searches under any spelling (Bhanabasti, Bhana Basti, भानाबस्ती, भाना बस्ती) — it appears to be a very small basti/hamlet, not a standalone revenue village, since it is absent from both the official Census2011 list (125 villages, Lunkaransar tehsil) and the MapsOfIndia village directory for the tehsil. The one substantive lead is a Jatland search-snippet stating Bhanabasti was founded by/named after 'Bhana', paternal uncle (tau) of one Nathu Dhatarwal — consistent with the unit's Dhatarwal-community note — but jatland.com blocks all automated fetches (403/bot-check on every jatland URL tried: /home/Lunkaransar, /home/Mahajan, /home/Bhanabasti), so this could not be verified beyond the search-engine summary and should be manually checked by a human researcher. A 2022 Patrika feature on Mahajan Field Firing Range displacement (34 villages, 1984-85 acquisition) names other villages (Bhojrasur, Kumbhana, Motlai, etc.) but not Bhanabasti by name — recorded for regional/displacement context only, not direct mention. Note a village-count discrepancy worth flagging: ConnectRajasthan lists Lunkaransar tehsil as having 139 villages while Wikipedia/Census2011 list 125 — Bhanabasti may fall in the gap as an unlisted/merged basti. This session's shared WebSearch budget (200 calls, apparently shared across other concurrent activity) was exhausted after only 6 searches for this unit, well short of the 25 allotted — remaining Tier 2/3 queries (temple/fair, school, land acquisition, gotra/family, video, social, image, book/archive queries) were NOT run and should be retried by a human or a future session with fresh budget.
